sources.name: Global Carbon Budget 2025: national fossil CO2 (territorial, consumption-based, transfers), national land-use change CO2, and global budget
sources.publisher: Global Carbon Project (GCP), coordinated by Univ. of Exeter / CICERO / ICOS Carbon Portal
sources.measures: Fossil CO2 emissions by country (territorial and consumption-based, plus emissions transferred through trade), land-use change (LUC) CO2 by country, and the global budget (fossil emissions, LUC emissions, atmospheric growth, ocean sink, land sink, cement carbonation sink, budget imbalance). Units are MtC or GtC per year; multiply by 3.664 to get CO2.
sources.coverage: Global budget 1750-2024 (fossil) and 1850-2024 (LUC and sinks). National territorial fossil emissions 1850-2024 for about 220 countries plus international aviation and shipping. Consumption-based emissions 1990-2023. Annual resolution. Also gridded 2015-2024 decadal-mean netCDF files.
sources.latest_release: GCB 2025. Data released 13 Nov 2025 (v0.1); final data v1.0 deposited on ICOS 17 May 2026; ESSD paper published 13 May 2026 (ESSD 18, 3211-3288). I checked China, USA, India and World for 2023-2024 and the values are identical in v0.1 and v1.0. GCB 2026 is expected around COP31 (9-20 Nov 2026) and is not out yet.
sources.update_cadence: Annual, in November, with the paper and the ICOS v1.0 data following about 6 months later.
sources.format: XLSX workbooks (sheets: Summary, Territorial Emissions, Consumption Emissions, Emissions Transfers, Regions; the global file has Global Carbon Budget, Historical Budget, Fossil Emissions by Category, Land-Use Change Emissions, Atmospheric Growth, Ocean Sink, Terrestrial Sink, Cement Carbonation Sink) and netCDF for gridded data
sources.license: The ICOS deposit is under the ICOS CCBY4 Data Licence, i.e. CC BY 4.0 (https://www.icos-cp.eu/data-services/about-data-portal/data-license). Key terms: "You must give appropriate credit, provide a link to the licence, and indicate if changes were made." The XLSX Summary sheet adds: "The use of data is conditional on citing the original data sources", and asks researchers to consider offering co-authorship. The ESSD article itself is CC BY 4.0.
sources.citation: Data: Global Carbon Project. (2026). Supplemental data of Global Carbon Budget 2025 (Version 1.0) [Data set]. Global Carbon Project. https://doi.org/10.18160/gcp-2025. Paper: Friedlingstein, P., O'Sullivan, M., Jones, M. W., et al.: Global Carbon Budget 2025, Earth Syst. Sci. Data, 18, 3211-3288, https://doi.org/10.5194/essd-18-3211-2026, 2026.
sources.status: Active. This is the 20th edition. It is not a US-federal product, although NOAA atmospheric data feeds into it.
sources.url_check: Fetched the GCB data-hub page, which lists the xlsx and netCDF links. The ICOS collection page shows 'Data supplement to the Global Carbon Budget 2025', v1.0, with the citation quoted above. The ICOS object pages show v1.0 published 17 May 2026 under the ICOS CCBY4 licence, and mark v0.1 (13 Nov 2025) as deprecated. A plain GET to data.icos-cp.eu returns 302 to licence_accept; with the CpLicenseAcceptedFor cookie it returns 200 with an XLSX of 755,198 bytes. globalcarbonbudget.org/download/2345 returns 200 with an XLSX of 739,007 bytes. I parsed both in memory: Territorial Emissions, World 2024 = 10,534.546 MtC; China 3,353.99; USA 1,338.46; India 871.58 (identical in both). I also parsed the Global Carbon Budget sheet: 2024 fossil excluding carbonation = 10.5345 GtC, LUC 1.2515, atmospheric growth 7.9225, ocean sink 3.3889, land sink 1.9422, cement carbonation sink 0.2243. The ESSD article page shows CC BY 4.0, published 13 May 2026.
sources.site_use: Core backbone for CO2. It drives: (1) the global source and sink 'bathtub' chart (emissions in = atmosphere + ocean + land); (2) country territorial vs consumption-based CO2 and trade transfers; (3) country LUC CO2 and fossil + LUC totals; (4) cumulative and historical-responsibility charts. Ingest the ICOS v1.0 files at build time and store the file hash, DOI and retrieval date in a provenance manifest.
sources.caveats: The GCB headline fossil figure (37.8 GtCO2 for 2024) is net of the cement carbonation sink (0.224 GtC, about 0.82 GtCO2). The national sheets and the Andrew & Peters CSV sum to 38.6 GtCO2 because they exclude that sink, so always label which one you show. Values are stored in carbon units. Each edition revises the history, so never mix editions. National LUC values have large uncertainty (global ELUC 1.3 ± 0.7 GtC). Consumption-based data lag one year (latest is 2023). The 2025 figures are projections: the press release says +1.1% (38.1 GtCO2), the final ESSD paper says +1.0%. ICOS downloads need the licence-cookie step.

drilldown_paths: THE BATHTUB (cause → consequence): fossil + land-use emissions → where the CO2 goes (atmosphere ~half, ocean, land) → concentration rising (Keeling curve) → warming. Data: GCB 2025 Global_Carbon_Budget xlsx, sheet 'Global Carbon Budget' (fossil, LUC, atmospheric growth, ocean sink, land sink, carbonation, imbalance 1959-2024); NOAA co2_annmean_gl and co2_mm_mlo; Jones GMST_response GLOBAL.

WORLD → GAS → SECTOR → ASSET: total GHG 2025 → CO2 / CH4 / N2O / F-gas → sector (power, transport, buildings, industry, fuel production, agriculture, waste) → subsector → individual power plants, oil fields and steel mills on a map → the asset's reduction strategies. Data: EDGAR 2026 booklet (GHG_by_sector_and_country, CH4/N2O CC BY), Climate TRACE v7 API (rankings/countries?sectors=..., /sources, ers_plan_global), PRIMAP-hist v2.8 for 1750+ sector history.

WORLD → FUEL → COUNTRY → PERSON: fossil CO2 → coal / oil / gas / cement / flaring → country map and ranking → per capita → consumption-based vs territorial ('what you import'). Data: GCP fossil CO2 2025v15 flat CSV (Total, Coal, Oil, Gas, Cement, Flaring, Other, Per Capita), GCB 2025 national xlsx (Territorial, Consumption, Emissions Transfers sheets), OWID owid-co2-data.csv for per-capita and consumption columns.

RESPONSIBILITY OVER TIME: annual emissions → cumulative since 1750 (fossil, then + land use) → each country's share → °C of warming caused (CO2 vs CH4 vs N2O; fossil vs land) → remaining 1.5°C budget countdown. Data: GCP v15 cumulative sums, GCB national LUC xlsx, OWID share_global_cumulative_*, Jones et al. 2025.1 GMST_response and EMISSIONS_CUMULATIVE_CO2e100, GCB 2025 remaining budget (170 GtCO2).

METHANE (fastest lever on near-term warming): atmospheric CH4 rising (NOAA) → sources budget with uncertainty (fossil 115, agriculture & waste 228, wetlands; Tg/yr) → national CH4 by sector (EDGAR CH4 / PRIMAP-hist) → fossil-fuel methane by country and leak intensity (IEA GMT 2026: 124 Mt; China, US, Russia lead) → Global Methane Pledge coverage. Data: NOAA ch4_annmean_gl, GCP-CH4 2024 xlsx (ICOS), EDGAR_CH4_1970_2025, IEA GMT 2026.

FOOD SYSTEM: share of all GHG from agrifood (31.7%) → farm gate vs land-use change vs pre/post-production → livestock (enteric fermentation, manure) / rice / fertilizer / deforestation / household food waste → by country → per-kg footprint of foods (beef vs beans). Data: FAOSTAT GT, GLE, GCE, GF, GPP bulk CSVs; Poore & Nemecek via OWID (pending licence).

LAND & FORESTS: land-use change CO2 globally (GCB ELUC 1.25 GtC in 2024) → by country (Brazil, Indonesia, DRC) → net forest conversion vs forest sink → cumulative CO2 including land use (Brazil jumps from 1.0% to 5.1% of the cumulative total). Data: GCB national LUC xlsx, FAOSTAT GF and GT ('Net Forest conversion', 'Forestland'), OWID share_global_cumulative_luc_co2, Climate TRACE forestry-and-land-use.

UNITED STATES DEEP DIVE (with the data-gap story): US total 1990-2024 → sector → key categories (#1 road transport CO2 1,451 MMT) → state → facilities near you (GHGRP RY2023) → the EPA inventory not published since 2024 and GHGRP RY2024 unreleased. Data: UMD CGS GHGIA 1990-2024 CSVs (DRUM), EPA GHGRP Envirofacts/FLIGHT RY2023, EPA 1990-2023 FOIA edition (EDF), Climate TRACE US assets 2024-2026.

OFFICIAL vs INDEPENDENT ('who is telling the truth?'): for a country, compare government-reported inventory (Tidy GHG Inventories / PRIMAP HISTCR) with independent estimates (GCB, EDGAR, Climate TRACE), with clear labels for differences in GWP, LULUCF and bunkers. Data: Tidy-GHG-Inventories-v2.1-long.xlsx, PRIMAP-hist v2.8 HISTCR vs HISTTP, EDGAR 2026, Climate TRACE.
research.action_links: INDIVIDUALS: (1) The per-capita and consumption-based views (GCP v15 and GCB 2025 'Consumption Emissions'; e.g. UK consumption footprint 7.1 t vs 4.5 t territorial) show that what we buy matters as much as where we live. (2) Transport is about 16% of global GHG (EDGAR 2026) and road transport is the single largest US category (1,451 MMT CO2e in 2024, UMD GHGIA Figure ES-2). (3) The food system is about 32% of global GHG (FAOSTAT GT 2023), with livestock and deforestation as the biggest pieces, so diet and food waste are direct levers. Product footprints come from Poore & Nemecek 2018 (licence pending). (4) IPCC AR6 WGIII SPM C.10 (https://www.ipcc.ch/report/ar6/wg3/chapter/summary-for-policymakers/) finds that demand-side measures (buildings, land transport, food) can cut end-use-sector emissions by 40-70% by 2050 compared with baseline scenarios. The figure data are reportedly CC BY 4.0 under DOI 10.48490/f0z3-n524; I could not reach the IPCC data browser to verify. COMMUNITIES: (5) Climate TRACE asset maps (CC BY 4.0) and EPA GHGRP RY2023 facility data (public domain) let residents identify the largest local emitters and their parent companies, for use in permitting hearings, utility rate cases and local methane-leak advocacy. (6) Power is about 29% of global GHG (EDGAR 2026 / Climate TRACE 2025), so community choice energy and utility decarbonisation are high-leverage. POLICYMAKERS: (7) Methane: IEA Global Methane Tracker 2026 (CC BY 4.0) reports 124 Mt a year from fossil fuel operations; 159 countries plus the EU have joined the Global Methane Pledge (a 30% cut by 2030), covering about 65% of sectoral methane. (8) The remaining 1.5°C budget is 170 GtCO2, about 4 years at current rates (GCB 2025), which frames how fast NDCs must cut emissions. (9) Data transparency: the US missed its 2025 and 2026 UNFCCC inventory submissions and GHGRP is proposed for elimination (EPA, Sep 2025 proposal). Showing that gap is itself an action item for citizens contacting representatives. Every action card should link to the exact dataset row behind its number.
research.gaps_and_risks: LICENSING: (a) PRIMAP-hist moved to CC BY-NC-SA 4.0. The record text says 'since v2.8', but the Zenodo license field already reads NC-SA for v2.7. Fine for a non-commercial site, but derived CSVs must carry the same licence. Alternatively pin v2.6.1, the last CC BY version (data to 2023). (b) EDGAR's fossil CO2 component (IEA-EDGAR CO2) is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, and it is embedded in EDGAR's GHG and sector totals. ND arguably blocks recomputed shares or per-capita values. Either get IEA permission (compliance@iea.org) or source the sector split from Climate TRACE (CC BY) and fossil CO2 from GCB (CC BY). EDGAR CH4, N2O and F-gas are CC BY. (c) Climate Watch's energy subsectors derive from IEA, and I could not read its permissions page, so avoid redistributing them. (d) The Carbon Majors terms forbid republishing and derivatives, so permission is needed. (e) The IEA Methane Tracker database licence (reported CC BY-SA) is unverified because iea.org returns 403. (f) Poore & Nemecek licence is unclear. (g) GCB xlsx and ICOS downloads need a licence-accept cookie (scriptable); cite the ICOS CC BY 4.0 deposit. COMPARABILITY: GCB fossil CO2 appears as 38.6 Gt (gross) or 37.8 Gt (net of cement carbonation). EDGAR uses AR5 GWP100 and includes bunkers, while PRIMAP-hist and Climate TRACE use AR6 and PRIMAP excludes bunkers. Totals differ with and without LULUCF. Climate TRACE totals swing with forestry (59.9 Gt in 2024 vs 54.4 Gt in 2025). Never mix sources in one chart without a label, and store the GWP basis, LULUCF flag and bunker flag in the provenance manifest. OWID: CO2 values are byte-identical to GCB (verified), but OWID total_ghg, methane and nitrous_oxide are OWID conversions of Jones et al. tonnages (AR6 GWP100: CH4 fossil 29.8, land 27.2, N2O 273), and OWID region and income aggregates are OWID-defined, so cite them as 'processed by OWID'. TIMELINESS: GCB 2026 and Jones 2026 are expected around COP31 (9-20 Nov 2026), so plan a re-ingest and keep old vintages addressable so published numbers stay traceable. The Global Methane Budget ends in 2020. Consumption-based data end in 2023. FAOSTAT and Climate Watch end in 2023. US FEDERAL RISK: the EPA national inventory has not been officially published since the 1990-2022 edition, and the 1990-2023 edition exists only via EDF FOIA. GHGRP RY2024 data were collected but not released (the Envirofacts API returns empty for 2024), and the program faces proposed elimination of 46 of 47 categories. NOAA GML survived the FY2026 appropriations but remains politically exposed. Mirror every upstream file (with SHA-256 hashes) in your own storage at build time. UNFCCC: the GHG Data Interface is stale (to 2021), so use Tidy GHG Inventories or the CRT originals. UNCERTAINTY: LUC per country (±0.7 GtC globally), the methane budget (top-down 575 vs bottom-up 669 Tg), and Jones warming attributions (no aerosols) need visible uncertainty or caveats. NOT YET REVIEWED (candidates): Global N2O Budget (Tian et al. 2024, ESSD 16:2543, data doi:10.18160/RQ8P-2Z4R); Energy Institute Statistical Review 2026 (energy domain); CEDS; IPCC AR6 WGIII figure data (data browser unreachable).

verdicts.name: Climate TRACE Emissions Inventory v5.11.0
verdicts.corrections: Confirmed: /data shows 'September release 5.11.0 includes monthly emissions data through July 2026' and API v7. The API reproduces the claimed numbers: 2025 total 54.418 Gt (China 16.60, USA 6.35, India 4.46); power 15.996; 2024 total 59.912. The terms page carries the CC BY 4.0 text. CORRECTIONS: (1) The terms exclude EDGAR-sourced country-level estimates for 'Other energy use, Railways, Other transportation, Other onsite fuel usage, Other Solid fuels, Other fossil fuel operations, Other manufacturing, Solid waste disposal, Biological treatment of solid waste, Incineration and open burning of waste, Fluorinated gases'. They also exclude FAOSTAT-sourced subsectors (rice in some geographies, other agricultural soils, enteric and manure 'other', other onsite fuel usage). So the country and sector totals from /rankings/countries are not purely CC BY. The fluorinated-gases sector (1.74 Gt) is entirely EDGAR. Calling Climate TRACE 'the CC BY alternative to EDGAR for sector splits' is overstated: only asset-level, Climate TRACE-modelled subsectors are cleanly CC BY. (2) A DOI does exist. Zenodo concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.15014790 holds versioned archives (CC BY 4.0); the latest archived is V5.10.0, 10.5281/zenodo.22919723, 2026-08-27. The record the researcher cited (19952746) is V5.5.0 (2026-03-26), and v5.11.0 is not yet on Zenodo. For activist traceability, pin the Zenodo version DOI rather than the live API. (3) The 2024 to 2025 drop comes entirely from forestry-and-land-use (+2.33 Gt in 2024 versus -3.38 Gt in 2025). Every other sector moved by less than 2%: power 15.94 to 16.0, transport 9.37 to 9.52, manufacturing 10.24 to 10.15. (4) See the headline check: the 29.4% power share mixes in net forestry.

The ICOS v1.0 'Global Carbon Budget' sheet gives (10.5345 - 0.2243 GtC) x 3.664 = 37.78 GtCO2; the ESSD abstract says '37.8 ± 1.8 GtCO2'. For 2025, the peer-reviewed ESSD value is +1.0% (0.2-1.7%) to 38.1 GtCO2; the +1.1% is the press release. Use +1.0%.
2) Half of all fossil CO2 emitted since 1996: CONFIRMED. Cumulative 1750-2024 = 1,849,123.9 MtCO2; the 50% mark is crossed in 1996; 57.58% has been emitted since 1990.
3) Cumulative shares: CONFIRMED (owid-co2-data.csv 2024). USA 23.517, EU27 16.273, China 15.417, Russia 6.641, UK 4.331, India 3.573. Including LUC: USA 20.372, China 13.071, Brazil 5.068 (fossil-only 0.984), Indonesia 3.160.

5) All GHG 54.1 GtCO2e in 2025: CONFIRMED. EDGAR booklet GLOBAL TOTAL 2025 = 54,149.17 and 2024 = 53,769.63 (+0.71%). The report_2026 page states 54.1 Gt, +0.7% / 380 Mt, and gas shares 73.8 / 17.6 / 5.3 / 3.3% verbatim. Context: IGCC 2025 (Forster et al. 2026) reports 56.8 ± 5.5 GtCO2e in 2024 including LULUCF, so label the basis (AR5 GWP, excluding LULUCF).
6) Sector split: the EDGAR shares are CONFIRMED by parsing the booklet for 2025: Power 15,811.4 (29.2%), Transport 8,770.7 (16.2%), Agriculture 6,322.7 (11.7%), Industrial Combustion 6,253.5 (11.5%), Fuel Production 6,105.0 (11.3%), Processes 5,378.9 (9.9%), Buildings 3,570.8 (6.6%), Waste 1,936.2 (3.6%). The Climate TRACE cross-check is CORRECTED. Its 15.996 / 54.418 = 29.4% divides by a total that includes net forestry of -3.38 Gt. Like-for-like (excluding forestry, as EDGAR excludes LULUCF), the total is 57.80 Gt and power is 27.7%. Note also that EDGAR sector shares are derived from IEA-EDGAR CO2 (NC-ND), and part of Climate TRACE's totals is EDGAR-sourced.
7) Food system about one third: CONFIRMED. 16,535,072 / 52,105,734 kt = 31.7% (FAOSTAT GT 2023). Caveat: the denominator nets LULUCF (only +0.47 Gt over the excluding-LULUCF total of 51,639,008), while the numerator includes 3.19 Gt of gross agrifood land-use change. On an 'excluding LULUCF + agrifood LUC' basis the share is 30.2%. Still 'about a third'.
8) Warming attributable to countries: CONFIRMED exactly. GLOBAL 1.67836, USA 0.29625 (17.7%), CHN 0.21737 (13.0%), EU27 0.17543 (10.5%), RUS 0.11794 (7.0%). For the aerosol caveat, cite IGCC 2025: human-induced warming 1.37°C in 2025 (decade 2016-2025: 1.24°C).

The final GCB 2025 ESSD abstract says '425.6 ppm in 2025, 53 % above pre-industrial levels'; the 52% (with 425.7 ppm) is from the 13 Nov 2025 press release. Arithmetic check: 425.62 / 278 = 1.531.

The researcher's note '50 GtC x 3.664 ≈ 183' misreads it: the abstract states both units, and the GtC figure is rounded. The press release also says 4.1 GtCO2 LUC in 2025, so 170 / 42.2 = 4.0 years. HOWEVER, the IPCC-method update IGCC 2025 (Forster et al. 2026, ESSD 18:3889, doi 10.5194/essd-18-3889-2026, CC BY 4.0) gives 'RCB estimate of 130 GtCO2 (50 % likelihood)' from the beginning of 2026, 'exhausted in a little more than 3 years' at 42 GtCO2/yr. Do not present 170 alone; show both with sources, or adopt one and footnote the other.
